Creator / Handle: 0 Seconds of Diamond School - Carbon Spot Diamond Knowledge - A Carbon Spot Doesn't Simply Expand Or Grow Like Stain - Fracture Associated With Inclusion Can Propagate - Dark Inclusion May Remain Same Size While Nearby Fracture Extends Branches Opens - Viewing Angle Lighting - Not Every Diamond With Dark Inclusion Automatically Durability Concern Type Location Relationship Matter - www.thediamondfrequency.co
Core Idea / 1-Line Takeaway: 0 Seconds of Diamond School—A carbon spot in a diamond doesn't simply expand or grow like a stain What can happen however is that a fracture associated with an inclusion can propagate through the diamond This can make the original inclusion appear larger over time leading to the impression that the carbon spot itself has expanded The distinction is important A dark inclusion may remain exactly the same size while a nearby fracture extends branches or opens slightly Depending on viewing angle and lighting that can change the way the inclusion appears to the eye This is also why not every diamond with a dark inclusion is automatically a durability concern The type location and relationship between inclusions and fractures matter when evaluating the stone So if you notice what looks like a growing carbon spot don't assume the carbon itself is expanding Rule Diamond knowledge on my website www.thediamondfrequency.co - KNOWLEDGE carbon spot fracture inclusion propagation durability

Post Type: Marketing & Branding + Entrepreneur + Sales - Wholesale Pricing Formula - Cost Is Starting Point Not Retail - Retail First Panic Half - Get Stocked
Core Idea / 1-Line Takeaway: Most jewellers price retail first, and then panic when a shop asks for half. Here's what usually happens. You look at what similar pieces sell for, land on £45, and put it in your shop. Then a shop asks for wholesale, you halve it to £22.50, and it barely covers your materials and your time. So you decide wholesale isn't for you. But retail was never the starting point. Your cost is. Here's order with numbers: Materials £8. Your time 45 minutes at £15 so £11. A share of your overheads £2. That's £21 to make. Wholesale is your cost times 2 so £42. Retail is your wholesale times 2 so £84. And here's bit that changes everything: Shop's half comes out of £84. It never comes out of your £42. You didn't lose half your price. You built their half into it from start! You still get £42 and that was always your number. A shop's 50% isn't taken from your price. It's built into it. And if maths doesn't work? If doubling your cost gives you retail price nobody would pay, that's genuinely useful information. It means your cost is too high, or piece is too slow to make. That's a making problem, not a shop problem. And it's fixable. Prices that hold up at wholesale are one of first things we fix inside Get Stocked, because everything else rests on them. Applications close this Friday 28 August and we start on 1st.
My Action - How I Will Use It: Wholesale Pricing Formula Cost First Framework

Core Idea / 1-Line Takeaway: The people who are scrolling past your posts are bombarded with options. Even if you have great engagement on your posts, people probably love what you have to offer, but if your content doesn't make them feel something, you're basically wasting time. So if you struggle to get likes turning into sales, here's what's actually happening. When someone scrolls past your post and thinks that's beautiful, you've done half the job. You got their attention. But attention is not desire. Desire is triggered by buyer psychology. The desire for significance, status, or feeling special. The desire for belonging or connection to a piece (can be fitting in with the group or connected emotionally to the piece). The desire for variety or to look different than everyone else. The desire to feel like their dollars are going to a good cause. The desire to feel like their identity is elevated by wearing it (ie more confidence, pulled together, stylish, beautiful) Before you post anything, ask yourself three questions: Does this create emotion? Can she see herself wearing it? Does it say something about who she is? And I'd love to help you create the type of content that actually moves people to buy your products.
